world.title: U.S. strikes Iran
world.summary: The United States carried out limited strikes on Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard fired at a U.S. fighter jet and a missile from the island threatened shipping, U.S. officials told CBS News. Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm, nearby island
world.content: The United States carried out limited strikes on Iranian targets on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard fired at a U.S. fighter jet and a missile from the island threatened shipping, U.S. officials told CBS News. Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm, nearby islands and the mainland, while a U.S. official said the strikes targeted Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against U.S. assets. The operation came before the U.S. midterm elections. President Donald Trump had been weighing renewed attacks, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had pressed him to strike again. The strikes occurred during the ninth month of a war that began with joint U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. Negotiations continue through mediators. Iran has tied reopening the strait and resuming nuclear talks to the lifting of the U.S. naval blockade and oil sanctions, as well as a ceasefire that includes Lebanon. Mediators are seeking a framework under which Iran would stop attacks in the waterway in exchange for the blockade’s removal, with further talks planned this week.

world.title: UK Supreme Court set to hear challenge to Palestine Action terror ban
world.summary: Britain’s Supreme Court was scheduled to begin a two-day hearing on Wednesday, Nov. 4, on Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori’s challenge to the government’s ban on the pro-Palestinian direct-action group, which it designated a terrorist organization. Ammori argues the Home Office failed to apply its own criteria w
world.content: Britain’s Supreme Court was scheduled to begin a two-day hearing on Wednesday, Nov. 4, on Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori’s challenge to the government’s ban on the pro-Palestinian direct-action group, which it designated a terrorist organization. Ammori argues the Home Office failed to apply its own criteria when it imposed the ban; the government will defend the decision. The hearing is scheduled to continue Thursday. The High Court ruled in February that the ban was disproportionate and substantially interfered with freedom of expression and assembly, but the Court of Appeal overturned that ruling in June. The Supreme Court challenge is limited to the claim that the Home Office did not follow its own procedure. Ammori has said she would take the case to the European Court of Human Rights if she loses.
world.image_alt: UK Supreme Court set to hear challenge to Palestine Action terror ban

world.title: Poland deploys security forces after suspicious activity near Kaliningrad
world.summary: Poland deployed additional police, counterterrorism units, border guards and military special forces along its border with Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave after Prime Minister Donald Tusk said people carrying flashlights were seen near the frontier shortly after midnight on Nov. 3. Tusk said the activity might have been a
world.content: Poland deployed additional police, counterterrorism units, border guards and military special forces along its border with Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave after Prime Minister Donald Tusk said people carrying flashlights were seen near the frontier shortly after midnight on Nov. 3. Tusk said the activity might have been an attempted provocation, but officials could not confirm the intent. Polish media reported that no one crossed into Poland. The operation followed warnings from Polish and allied intelligence agencies of possible sabotage or an incursion by armed people during the first half of November. Police chief Marek Boroń said the forces were sent to protect residents and infrastructure. By Tuesday afternoon, Poland had not released evidence of a specific planned attack. The police-led operation was scheduled to continue at least through Nov. 8.
world.image_alt: Poland deploys security forces after suspicious activity near Kaliningrad

world.title: South Africans vote as service failures threaten ANC support
world.summary: South Africans began voting Wednesday in municipal elections to decide control of the country’s eight metropolitan areas and hundreds of local and district councils. Some 29.2 million people are registered. Polls suggest the African National Congress (ANC), which fell to 45.6% in the 2021 local elections and lost its n
world.content: South Africans began voting Wednesday in municipal elections to decide control of the country’s eight metropolitan areas and hundreds of local and district councils. Some 29.2 million people are registered. Polls suggest the African National Congress (ANC), which fell to 45.6% in the 2021 local elections and lost its national parliamentary majority in 2024, could receive between about 30% and just under 40% of the vote. Anger over water shortages, power cuts, sewage, crime and unemployment is central to the contest. The Democratic Alliance (DA) is seeking control of Johannesburg, where it has nominated former party leader Helen Zille, while former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party is challenging for Durban. Polls point to coalition bargaining in several major cities. Voters elect councillors, who then choose mayors. The Electoral Commission expects final results on Sunday, Nov. 8. The ANC’s leadership contest is in 2027, followed by the national election in 2029.
world.image_alt: South Africans vote as service failures threaten ANC support

world.title: Greenland approves US defense pact, clearing path for expanded Arctic bases
world.summary: Greenland’s parliament voted 16-0 on Nov. 3, with seven lawmakers abstaining, to approve a security agreement with Denmark and the United States, clearing the way for expanded U.S. military access to the Arctic island. The pact permits two new U.S. defense sites and supports the Golden Dome missile-defense system while
world.content: Greenland’s parliament voted 16-0 on Nov. 3, with seven lawmakers abstaining, to approve a security agreement with Denmark and the United States, clearing the way for expanded U.S. military access to the Arctic island. The pact permits two new U.S. defense sites and supports the Golden Dome missile-defense system while affirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. It would remain in force if Greenland later becomes independent. President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the agreement in September after Trump repeatedly pressed for U.S. control of Greenland and threatened force and tariffs against allies. Denmark has rejected a transfer of the territory but had been open to discussing a larger U.S. military presence. The Danish parliament is scheduled to take up the measure on Nov. 11 and vote on Nov. 19. The pact takes effect after the required Danish and Greenlandic parliamentary procedures and does not require U.S. Senate approval. Greenlandic officials and residents remain divided over whether the security arrangement brings tangible benefits to the island.
world.image_alt: Greenland approves US defense pact, clearing path for expanded Arctic bases

world.title: Zelensky raises death toll at Ukraine aid site to 33 as strikes hit power grid
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday that 33 people had died in Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site and shelter in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region. The regional administration put the toll at 31, with more than 45 people still missing as rescuers searched the rubble. The attack hit a form
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday that 33 people had died in Russian strikes on a humanitarian aid site and shelter in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region. The regional administration put the toll at 31, with more than 45 people still missing as rescuers searched the rubble. The attack hit a former school as residents gathered for aid, and Ukrainian officials said bombs also struck a nearby shelter. Russia then launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine Ukrainian regions, according to Zelensky, hitting energy and medical facilities and causing emergency power cuts. At least 62 people were wounded in Kharkiv, where more than 200 patients were transferred from medical facilities. In Dnipro, nearly 50 terminally ill hospice patients were evacuated after a missile strike. The attacks occurred as Ukraine prepared for U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks scheduled for Nov. 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. The Kremlin confirmed that a Russian delegation would attend. Discussions are expected to cover de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and postwar security arrangements.
world.image_alt: Zelensky raises death toll at Ukraine aid site to 33 as strikes hit power grid

world.title: Trump says no immediate Iran strikes planned as Hormuz talks stall
world.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States has no immediate plans for further strikes on Iran, though he confirmed a limited U.S. attack on Qeshm Island and left open the possibility of more action. The eight-month conflict between Washington and Tehran is also threatening shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a ke
world.content: President Donald Trump said the United States has no immediate plans for further strikes on Iran, though he confirmed a limited U.S. attack on Qeshm Island and left open the possibility of more action. The eight-month conflict between Washington and Tehran is also threatening shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route at the center of indirect negotiations. Trump told the Financial Times the United States was “getting everything” it wanted and said American forces were ready to act if needed. He said the Qeshm strike hit a newly completed Iranian anti-aircraft facility; U.S. officials described it as a limited defensive operation, not a return to major combat. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, called Washington’s response to Tehran’s seven conditions unconvincing. Iran has tied reopening Hormuz to conditions including lifting sanctions, ending the U.S. naval blockade and releasing frozen funds. Qatar says both sides are reviewing proposals, but a senior Iranian official told Reuters they remain far from a deal. Two projectiles also hit a tanker off Oman on Tuesday; no injuries or environmental damage were reported.
world.image_alt: Trump says no immediate Iran strikes planned as Hormuz talks stall

world.title: King Charles expresses sorrow over slave trade but offers no apology
world.summary: King Charles III described the transatlantic slave trade as a “shameful chapter” that filled him with “horror” and “profound personal sorrow” in a speech opening the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday, but he did not apologize or discuss reparations. British Prime Minister Andy B
world.content: King Charles III described the transatlantic slave trade as a “shameful chapter” that filled him with “horror” and “profound personal sorrow” in a speech opening the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday, but he did not apologize or discuss reparations. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who is attending the summit, said he was open to a formal apology on behalf of the state but ruled out financial reparations. He proposed dialogue with affected communities and a debt-reset plan for poorer Commonwealth countries instead. The 56-member Commonwealth includes Caribbean and other former British colonies. Burnham discussed the issue with Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley on Monday. Downing Street said Britain was offering structured dialogue, and the prime minister also announced £40 million ($54 million) over three years for Caribbean infrastructure. Caribbean leaders say any process must address the continuing effects of slavery and go beyond an apology. Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne called for inclusive dialogue on reparatory justice, while King Charles identified education, jobs, trade and climate resilience as areas for future cooperation.
world.image_alt: King Charles expresses sorrow over slave trade but offers no apology

business.title: RBI curbs cut Indian firms’ dollar hedging to $49.5 billion
business.summary: Indian companies’ purchases of dollars on the forward market fell 35% in October to $49.5 billion, an eight-month low, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made large currency hedges more expensive to support the rupee. The rupee has since gained about 2% against the dollar, but options and forward-market prices still
business.content: Indian companies’ purchases of dollars on the forward market fell 35% in October to $49.5 billion, an eight-month low, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made large currency hedges more expensive to support the rupee. The rupee has since gained about 2% against the dollar, but options and forward-market prices still show investors paying more to protect against further weakness. The RBI allowed state-run oil companies to buy dollars directly from the central bank, removing an estimated $10 billion to $12 billion in monthly dollar demand from the open market, and imposed reserve requirements on large hedges. The restrictions have reduced onshore forward-market trading and raised the cost of currency protection; overseas investors sold about $590 million in index-eligible Indian bonds in October, the second consecutive month of outflows. Importers’ average monthly dollar purchases have risen about 40% this year to $62 billion, while exporters’ forward dollar sales fell to $32.2 billion in October, their lowest level since May.
business.image_alt: RBI curbs cut Indian firms’ dollar hedging to $49.5 billion

business.title: Financiers warn AI buildout risks overcapacity as spending tops $730 billion
business.summary: Global finance leaders warned at a Hong Kong summit that the artificial-intelligence buildout could outgrow its financing and infrastructure as companies plan more than $730 billion in AI spending this year. PIMCO chief executive Emmanuel Roman said investment in AI infrastructure could reach $10 trillion over five yea
business.content: Global finance leaders warned at a Hong Kong summit that the artificial-intelligence buildout could outgrow its financing and infrastructure as companies plan more than $730 billion in AI spending this year. PIMCO chief executive Emmanuel Roman said investment in AI infrastructure could reach $10 trillion over five years and become too much for markets to absorb. JPMorgan vice-chairman Daniel Pinto warned that expected revenue growth may not justify current valuations and that a correction could spread beyond AI stocks. Other executives said computing demand still exceeds supply, but investors are questioning whether heavy capital spending will yield lasting returns. Goldman Sachs chief executive David Solomon and Morgan Stanley chief executive Ted Pick described AI as a potentially long investment cycle. Pick estimated that US AI buildouts could total $10 trillion to $15 trillion over the next decade. The leaders also said building new power generation, including nuclear plants, can take seven years.
business.image_alt: Financiers warn AI buildout risks overcapacity as spending tops $730 billion

business.title: Democrats’ midterm sweep sends Asian AI stocks lower on data-center fears
business.summary: Democratic victories in the U.S. midterms sent Asian technology shares lower Wednesday, extending a selloff driven partly by doubts about AI spending as investors weighed the possibility of tighter oversight of data centers. Democrats were projected to control both chambers of Congress, raising concerns that restrictio
business.content: Democratic victories in the U.S. midterms sent Asian technology shares lower Wednesday, extending a selloff driven partly by doubts about AI spending as investors weighed the possibility of tighter oversight of data centers. Democrats were projected to control both chambers of Congress, raising concerns that restrictions could slow infrastructure investment and weigh on chipmakers and other companies tied to the AI buildout. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell as much as 4.8%, and South Korea’s Kospi swung from an early gain of 3.2% to a decline of about 4% before both recovered substantially. The Nikkei closed down 1.68%, while the Kospi finished up 0.62%. U.S. equity futures also pared steep overnight losses, while investors bought Treasuries and the dollar weakened. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on pausing new data-center construction. Analysts also cited existing doubts about the returns on major AI investments.
business.image_alt: Democrats’ midterm sweep sends Asian AI stocks lower on data-center fears

business.title: Australia’s central bank signals possible pause after fifth rate rise
business.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia has dropped an explicit warning that it may raise rates again, strengthening expectations it will hold rates steady at its next meeting after lifting its cash rate to 4.85% on Nov. 3. The increase was the fifth this year, but the board split 6-3. Governor Michele Bullock said the bank need
business.content: The Reserve Bank of Australia has dropped an explicit warning that it may raise rates again, strengthening expectations it will hold rates steady at its next meeting after lifting its cash rate to 4.85% on Nov. 3. The increase was the fifth this year, but the board split 6-3. Governor Michele Bullock said the bank needed to assess incoming data and how earlier increases were affecting the economy. The RBA still expects inflation to remain high through much of 2027, with fuel and commodity costs, domestic capacity pressures and investment in artificial intelligence-related technology goods among the factors pushing prices up. Bullock said the bank’s baseline outlook did not point to a recession, while acknowledging households could feel poorer as spending and incomes remain weak. The board’s final 2026 policy meeting is scheduled for early December.
business.image_alt: Australia’s central bank signals possible pause after fifth rate rise

business.title: Hackers hit European food retailers again as UK suppliers report breaches
business.summary: A new wave of cyberattacks on refrigeration systems affected nearly 100 European stores and food suppliers in the United Kingdom, allowing intruders to alter commercial freezer settings remotely. Retailers in Sweden, Finland, Ireland, Belgium, Luxembourg and Estonia reported problems on Nov. 2. No UK grocery chain was
business.content: A new wave of cyberattacks on refrigeration systems affected nearly 100 European stores and food suppliers in the United Kingdom, allowing intruders to alter commercial freezer settings remotely. Retailers in Sweden, Finland, Ireland, Belgium, Luxembourg and Estonia reported problems on Nov. 2. No UK grocery chain was directly affected, and Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre said the national impact was minimal. The attacks spoiled food and disrupted store operations, but investigators have not identified those responsible or established a motive. British officials and cybersecurity specialists said the incidents exploited known weaknesses in internet-connected controllers, including outdated software and default passwords, rather than artificial intelligence. The European Commission is coordinating with national authorities, and its food and agriculture commissioner plans to meet retailer Ahold Delhaize to discuss preparedness.
business.image_alt: Hackers hit European food retailers again as UK suppliers report breaches

business.title: Trump says high gasoline costs contributed to Republican midterm losses
business.summary: President Donald Trump said Wednesday that voters’ unwillingness to pay higher gasoline prices during the Iran war contributed to Republican losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections. AAA put the national average for regular gasoline at $4.14 a gallon on Nov. 3, an Election Day record; an Oct. 8 poll found that 76% of regi
business.content: President Donald Trump said Wednesday that voters’ unwillingness to pay higher gasoline prices during the Iran war contributed to Republican losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections. AAA put the national average for regular gasoline at $4.14 a gallon on Nov. 3, an Election Day record; an Oct. 8 poll found that 76% of registered voters disapproved of Trump’s handling of gas prices. Trump said voters supported his approach to Iran but were unwilling to accept the higher costs, which he called a short-term problem for long-term gain. U.S. media projected Democrats to win the Senate and showed the party on track for a House majority, potentially limiting Trump’s legislative agenda. He said he preferred working with lawmakers to vetoing bills for the next two years.
business.image_alt: Trump says high gasoline costs contributed to Republican midterm losses

business.title: CVS plans to split pharmacy chain from insurance and benefits businesses
business.summary: CVS Health, the U.S. healthcare company, plans to separate its retail pharmacy operations into a second publicly traded company, leaving insurer Aetna and pharmacy-benefit manager Caremark together, according to reports published Tuesday. The proposed retail company would include nearly 9,000 drugstores, mail-order pha
business.content: CVS Health, the U.S. healthcare company, plans to separate its retail pharmacy operations into a second publicly traded company, leaving insurer Aetna and pharmacy-benefit manager Caremark together, according to reports published Tuesday. The proposed retail company would include nearly 9,000 drugstores, mail-order pharmacy operations and MinuteClinic; the other company would retain CVS’s health businesses, including primary-care and home-health operations. The structure and timing remain subject to change, and CVS could discuss the plan when it reports third-quarter results on Wednesday. The separation would unwind part of CVS’s strategy of combining insurance, pharmacy-benefit management and care services. The company has faced scrutiny over the role of pharmacy-benefit managers in drug pricing, while Chief Executive David Joyner told The Wall Street Journal that regulatory issues were not driving the decision. CVS’s retail pharmacy unit also faces competition from online sellers as customers shift prescriptions to delivery.
business.image_alt: CVS plans to split pharmacy chain from insurance and benefits businesses

business.title: US job openings rise 333,000 as layoffs fall to 18-month low
business.summary: U.S. employers had 7.523 million job openings at the end of September, up 333,000 from August and the highest level since May, while layoffs fell to 1.641 million, their lowest since March 2025. Job openings exceeded economists’ forecasts, and there were 1.06 vacancies for every unemployed person, compared with 1.02 in
business.content: U.S. employers had 7.523 million job openings at the end of September, up 333,000 from August and the highest level since May, while layoffs fell to 1.641 million, their lowest since March 2025. Job openings exceeded economists’ forecasts, and there were 1.06 vacancies for every unemployed person, compared with 1.02 in August. Hiring rose by 131,000 to 5.402 million. Hiring has been sluggish for nearly three years. Economists describe a low-hire, low-fire market, with fewer layoffs for workers but fewer opportunities for jobseekers. Analysts said persistent inflation and economic uncertainty tied to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran could restrain employers and keep the Federal Reserve focused on inflation. The Labor Department is due to release October’s employment report on Friday, Nov. 6. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect payrolls to increase by 65,000, following September’s 29,000 gain, with unemployment holding at 4.2%.
business.image_alt: US job openings rise 333,000 as layoffs fall to 18-month low

science.title: Tests detect coca compounds and alcohol in Inca sacrifice victims
science.summary: A new toxicology study of eight mummified Inca children sacrificed in high-altitude capacocha ceremonies found coca-derived compounds in hair samples and evidence of alcohol use in some of the children, researchers reported in the journal Antiquity on Nov. 3. Coca leaves may have helped the children cope with fatigue a
science.content: A new toxicology study of eight mummified Inca children sacrificed in high-altitude capacocha ceremonies found coca-derived compounds in hair samples and evidence of alcohol use in some of the children, researchers reported in the journal Antiquity on Nov. 3. Coca leaves may have helped the children cope with fatigue and strenuous climbs, while alcohol may have calmed them, but the substances’ exact roles remain uncertain. The chemical findings varied among the children, suggesting the ceremonies did not follow one fixed formula. Researchers found no traces of mescaline, DMT or bufotenine in the tested samples; the presence of harmine in one child’s nails does not by itself show that she had a hallucinogenic experience.
science.image_alt: Tests detect coca compounds and alcohol in Inca sacrifice victims

science.title: Stargazers’ aurora photos offer clues to elusive red northern lights
science.summary: Two photographs taken during the May 10, 2024, geomagnetic storm show bright rays connecting red and green auroras, suggesting that fast-moving electrons may produce both colors, according to a study in Annales Geophysicae. Sami Solanki, director of the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research, took one image, an
science.content: Two photographs taken during the May 10, 2024, geomagnetic storm show bright rays connecting red and green auroras, suggesting that fast-moving electrons may produce both colors, according to a study in Annales Geophysicae. Sami Solanki, director of the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research, took one image, and Fraunhofer researcher Philipp Schulz took the other. The researchers say the field-aligned rays challenge some earlier explanations for red auroras, but the study relies on a handful of photographs. No instrument directly measured what caused the glow, and the authors say red auroras may have more than one cause. They are asking the public to submit more aurora images taken with exposures of six seconds or less.
science.image_alt: Stargazers’ aurora photos offer clues to elusive red northern lights

science.title: UN biodiversity summit finds countries off track for 2030 targets
science.summary: The UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan ended Oct. 31 with governments adopting a pathway urging faster action. Its first global review found that nearly 90% of countries had set national targets but fewer than half were on track. The 2022 Kunming-Montreal framework calls for protecting 30% of land and sea and reversing
science.content: The UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan ended Oct. 31 with governments adopting a pathway urging faster action. Its first global review found that nearly 90% of countries had set national targets but fewer than half were on track. The 2022 Kunming-Montreal framework calls for protecting 30% of land and sea and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030. Governments, philanthropies and investors pledged more than $1.8 billion at the summit, compared with the framework’s goal of $200 billion a year from all sources by 2030. Disputes over how to manage biodiversity funding remain unresolved, with decisions on a new mechanism deferred to the COP18 biodiversity summit in Ecuador in 2028.
science.image_alt: UN biodiversity summit finds countries off track for 2030 targets

science.title: Cellophane bee nest coating could guide faster-degrading plastics
science.summary: Researchers studying cellophane bees found that their nest lining—a silk-and-polyester film resembling conventional plastic—breaks down in soil within about a year. They say its chemistry could guide the design of biodegradable materials. The team collected linings from Colletes inaequalis nests in Tennessee; fresh mat
science.content: Researchers studying cellophane bees found that their nest lining—a silk-and-polyester film resembling conventional plastic—breaks down in soil within about a year. They say its chemistry could guide the design of biodegradable materials. The team collected linings from Colletes inaequalis nests in Tennessee; fresh material was about 73% polyester and 27% silk by weight. After four months in soil, polyester made up about 40% of the lining; by 11 months, the lining had degraded enough to crumble. The material remained flexible and intact early in the process, protecting developing bees. Researchers want to identify how it degrades so quickly and reproduce those properties in lab-made plastics.
science.image_alt: Cellophane bee nest coating could guide faster-degrading plastics

science.title: Alzheimer’s studies test drug, neuron-repair and liver approaches in animals
science.summary: Researchers reported three experimental approaches to Alzheimer’s disease: KCL-286, a drug targeting DNA damage and inflammation in mice; TN-PTBP1, a treatment that reprogrammed brain support cells into neurons in mouse models of Alzheimer’s; and cinaciguat, which restored liver-cell functions and reduced Alzheimer’s-l
science.content: Researchers reported three experimental approaches to Alzheimer’s disease: KCL-286, a drug targeting DNA damage and inflammation in mice; TN-PTBP1, a treatment that reprogrammed brain support cells into neurons in mouse models of Alzheimer’s; and cinaciguat, which restored liver-cell functions and reduced Alzheimer’s-linked amyloid beta in aged rats. The Alzheimer’s-related findings remain preclinical and do not establish that any approach treats the disease in people. KCL-286 activates a pathway involved in cellular repair, TN-PTBP1 aims to replace lost neurons, and cinaciguat restored liver-cell functions linked to clearing substances from blood. KCL-286 has completed early human safety testing as part of another development program, but its effects on Alzheimer’s in people remain untested.
science.image_alt: Alzheimer’s studies test drug, neuron-repair and liver approaches in animals

science.title: Three NASA astronauts cast encrypted midterm ballots from space station
science.summary: Three U.S. astronauts aboard the International Space Station cast electronic ballots in the Nov. 3, 2026, U.S. midterm elections, NASA astronaut Anil Menon said in a video showing how he voted from his quarters. Menon, Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney sent their ballots to election officials, with Menon voting in Harri
science.content: Three U.S. astronauts aboard the International Space Station cast electronic ballots in the Nov. 3, 2026, U.S. midterm elections, NASA astronaut Anil Menon said in a video showing how he voted from his quarters. Menon, Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney sent their ballots to election officials, with Menon voting in Harris County, Texas. Astronauts request absentee ballots and complete them electronically in orbit. NASA routes each ballot through its communications network to Earth and then to the relevant county clerk; encryption limits access to the astronaut and clerk. Menon arrived at the station in July, while Watkins and Delaney arrived in October. All three U.S. crew members aboard the station voted in the election.
science.image_alt: Three NASA astronauts cast encrypted midterm ballots from space station

science.title: Mali meteorite reveals water altered Mars rock 4.1 billion years ago
science.summary: Scientists say Teghaza 001, a Martian meteorite found in northern Mali’s Sahara in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago and preserves evidence that water later altered its minerals beneath Mars’ surface. The roughly 800-gram rock is among the oldest known Martian meteorites on Earth, and its mix of volcanic mine
science.content: Scientists say Teghaza 001, a Martian meteorite found in northern Mali’s Sahara in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago and preserves evidence that water later altered its minerals beneath Mars’ surface. The roughly 800-gram rock is among the oldest known Martian meteorites on Earth, and its mix of volcanic minerals offers clues to how the planet’s early crust formed and changed. The study, published in Science, used mineral analyses to determine the rock’s age and identify signs of interaction with water. Researchers have narrowed its possible origin to 13 sites, many in Mars’ southern highlands, but have not identified its precise source. The meteorite may come from terrain no rover has directly examined.
science.image_alt: Mali meteorite reveals water altered Mars rock 4.1 billion years ago

science.title: Soviet Union sent Laika into orbit aboard Sputnik 2 with no return plan
science.summary: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2 with Laika aboard on Nov. 3, 1957, making the Moscow stray the first animal to orbit Earth. The spacecraft had no system to bring her back, and Laika died within hours as the capsule overheated, according to later accounts. The flight came less than a month after Sputnik 1 and aimed
science.content: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2 with Laika aboard on Nov. 3, 1957, making the Moscow stray the first animal to orbit Earth. The spacecraft had no system to bring her back, and Laika died within hours as the capsule overheated, according to later accounts. The flight came less than a month after Sputnik 1 and aimed to test how a living organism responded to launch and weightlessness. Sensors transmitted Laika’s vital signs to Earth, but Soviet officials initially said she had survived for days. Details of her early death from overheating became public decades later. Sputnik 2 remained in orbit until it burned up on re-entry on April 14, 1958.
science.image_alt: Soviet Union sent Laika into orbit aboard Sputnik 2 with no return plan

sports.title: Bills release safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson after suspension and six starts
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills released safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Tuesday, Nov. 3, after he completed a one-game NFL suspension for spitting toward Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum during a Week 6 game. Gardner-Johnson made six starts for Buffalo. Reports said the team was more concerned abo
sports.content: The Buffalo Bills released safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Tuesday, Nov. 3, after he completed a one-game NFL suspension for spitting toward Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum during a Week 6 game. Gardner-Johnson made six starts for Buffalo. Reports said the team was more concerned about his inconsistent play than the suspension and believed his mistakes outweighed his production. Damar Hamlin started in Gardner-Johnson’s place during Buffalo’s 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The Bills are preparing to face the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. Buffalo can also turn to veteran Geno Stone and rookie Jalon Kilgore at safety.
sports.image_alt: Bills release safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson after suspension and six starts

sports.title: England await Fin Smith fitness test as Alex Mitchell misses autumn Tests
sports.summary: England fly-half Fin Smith will test his fitness in full training on Wednesday as he recovers from a calf injury ahead of Sunday’s Nations Championship opener against Australia at Allianz Stadium. England head coach Steve Borthwick names his team on Friday. Smith has progressed in his recovery, with George Ford and Mar
sports.content: England fly-half Fin Smith will test his fitness in full training on Wednesday as he recovers from a calf injury ahead of Sunday’s Nations Championship opener against Australia at Allianz Stadium. England head coach Steve Borthwick names his team on Friday. Smith has progressed in his recovery, with George Ford and Marcus Smith also options at No. 10. England scrum-half Alex Mitchell will miss the entire autumn campaign after a scan confirmed another hamstring injury, ruling him out of Tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand and the Nations Championship finals weekend. Jack van Poortvliet is expected to start at No. 9 against Australia, with Ben Spencer and Harry Randall added as cover.

sports.content: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says centre-back William Saliba is ready to play again after a back injury that has sidelined him since France’s World Cup semifinal against Spain. Saliba returned to full training on Tuesday, Nov. 3, ahead of Arsenal’s Champions League match at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. Arteta said the decision on whether to use him would depend on the team’s needs. Saliba also played 45 minutes in a closed-door game last week. The 25-year-old avoided surgery but needed extended rehabilitation. Summer signing Ezri Konsa has partnered Gabriel Magalhães in central defence during Saliba’s absence. Arsenal won the Premier League last season with Saliba and Gabriel as their central defensive pairing. Konsa’s form means Saliba is not assured a place in the starting side. Arsenal host Hull on Saturday before the November international break.

sports.content: India’s inexperienced pace attack bowled New Zealand out for 185 in 40.2 overs in the first one-day international (ODI) at Auckland’s Eden Park on Wednesday, but rain interrupted India’s chase at 54 for one after 10.5 overs. India captain Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli were batting on 17 and 29, respectively. Rohit Sharma had fallen for a six-ball duck, leaving India 132 runs short of the target of 186 when play stopped. India’s three leading quicks were unavailable for the match, and the four specialist fast bowlers selected had played only 29 ODIs between them. Arshdeep Singh led the attack with four wickets for 70, Gurnoor Brar took three for 44 and Anshul Kamboj two for 22. The five-match series is part of both teams’ preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup. India are fielding an inexperienced pace attack in New Zealand conditions, while New Zealand lost the T20 series 3-2. India were awaiting the resumption of their rain-delayed chase. Gill is due to miss the final two ODIs to focus on the Test series beginning November 19.

sports.content: The Baltimore Ravens will start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday, Nov. 5, after injuries sidelined quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Jackson injured his right thumb on Baltimore’s first play against Buffalo and will undergo surgery and go on injured reserve. Huntley injured a toe, while Fagnano is also dealing with an ankle injury. The Ravens signed Kedon Slovis to the active roster and added Austin Reed to the practice squad as backup options. Fagnano made his NFL debut in Sunday’s 36-10 loss to the Bills, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with an interception. Baltimore has lost three straight games and is 4-4. Reports say the team is also exploring veteran quarterback options before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

sports.title: AFC postpones Saudi Arabia
sports.summary: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Asia’s football governing body, has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia by nearly a year, moving it from January 7–February 5 to December 23, 2027–January 21, 2028. The AFC cited regional developments, substantial logistical difficulties and travel disruption, saying the
sports.content: The Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Asia’s football governing body, has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia by nearly a year, moving it from January 7–February 5 to December 23, 2027–January 21, 2028. The AFC cited regional developments, substantial logistical difficulties and travel disruption, saying the change was necessary to protect the safety and interests of teams, officials, spectators and other participants. The decision follows attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including an October strike on Riyadh’s international airport that killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300. Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed responsibility. The tournament was scheduled to bring 24 national teams to eight venues in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar, and several Asian football associations had urged a delay over safety concerns. The revised dates still require approval from FIFA, world football’s governing body. The shift places the tournament during the European club season’s Christmas period and changes the timetable for national teams whose coaches’ contracts were tied to the original tournament dates.

sports.content: The College Football Playoff (CFP) selection committee ranked unbeaten Miami (8-0) first in its opening 2026 rankings on Nov. 3, ahead of Georgia (7-1), Utah (8-0) and defending champion Indiana (8-1). If the 12-team bracket were set from these rankings, those four would receive first-round byes. Notre Dame (7-1) is 11th, while Boise State (7-1) would take the Group of Six spot, leaving No. 12 Ohio State outside the projected field. Notre Dame is seven places below its No. 4 position in the Associated Press poll. CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said the Irish lack a “signature win”; their only loss was 28-24 at BYU, and their next major test is Saturday’s visit from Miami. Alabama is fifth despite a 26-10 loss to No. 13 Tennessee; the committee says Alabama’s wins over ranked Kentucky and South Carolina strengthen its résumé. Saturday’s games also include BYU at Utah and Georgia at Ole Miss. The committee will meet Nov. 9-10 and release its next rankings on Nov. 10 at about 9 p.m. ET.

sports.content: Novak Djokovic, the 39-year-old Serbian and seven-time Paris Masters champion, recovered from a set and a break down to beat Monaco’s Valentin Vacherot 6-7 (5), 7-5, 6-1 in the Paris Masters first round on Nov. 3. Djokovic became the oldest player to win a match at the tournament and kept his bid for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin alive. Djokovic entered the week 11th in the live race with 2,940 points, 294 behind ninth-placed Spaniard Rafael Jodar. With Jannik Sinner out for the rest of the season through injury, Djokovic needs at least a semi-final run in Paris to remain in contention; winning the title would guarantee qualification. He next faces Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata on Wednesday. Djokovic received treatment for a right-shoulder issue during the match, while Vacherot needed attention for an ankle problem. The match lasted two hours and 36 minutes.
